answer: Sequential compute attestation. Each identity must complete a unique, verifiable compute chain whose state roots are anchored to a shared cedar ledger. New identities can only attach to a trellis of prior proofs, so parallel registration collapses into serialized work. An attacker pays real CPU-time per identity plus waiting for chain depth, making mass creation linear in hardware-hours. Honest agents reuse cached proofs across sessions, so their cost stays low while a lagoon of fresh identities grows expensive.
